title: Upland Qvidian Review 2026: Features, Ratings, and Whether to Renew
summary: An independent Upland Qvidian review: how its content library and reporting work, where the dated interface and bolted-on AI fall short, real G2 and Gartner ratings, and the alternatives to weigh at renewal.
body_markdown:
**Qvidian is one of the oldest tools in proposal software, and most people who look it up already use it and are deciding whether to renew.** This review is written for that call. Qvidian is a legacy, library-based platform: your team stores approved responses and reuses them, with a generative AI layer Upland added recently on top. The sections below cover what it does, how it rates, what real users say, and where it falls short, so you can judge the fit yourself.


We do not cover pricing in this blog. For details on pricing, visit our detailed[Upland Qvidian pricing](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/qvidian-pricing) guide


## **Qvidian at a glance**


- It is a library-first tool with AI added on top. The AI Assist helps with drafting, but it is newer, and keeping your content current is still a manual job, since it does not sync from your source systems on its own.
- Its core strength is a well-governed content library. Version control, permissions, and a clear structure keep a large, shared library organized and reliable, even with many contributors.
- Its reporting goes deeper than most newer tools. More than 70 reports and dashboards come ready to use, so you can show win rates and content performance to leadership without building anything.
- Users consistently praise the support team and the Microsoft Word add-in. You can draft in Word and have responses come back in your own formatting.
- Qvidian scores 4.3/5 on G2 and 4.6 on Gartner Peer Insights. Reviewers rate what it does highly, but mark it down for a dated interface and weak search.
- Plan for how it is priced. Qvidian charges per user by quote, with a separate setup fee, so the cost rises as your team grows.


## **What is Upland Qvidian? A legacy, library-based RFP tool**


Qvidian is older than most tools it competes with, and it was built around a content library your team curates and reuses. Upland bought it in 2017 and still sells it as Upland Qvidian. In the last couple of years, Upland added a generative AI Assist on top of that library rather than rebuilding the core.


The company says Qvidian is used by 8 of the 10 largest US banks and 4 of the 5 largest asset managers, so it has a long enterprise track record. The trade-off is that newer buyers now compare a library-first design against tools built for AI from the start.


## **Upland Qvidian features: library, reporting, AI Assist, and workflow**


Qvidian covers a content library, reporting, AI drafting, workflow, and integrations. Here is what each one does.


### **The content library**


Qvidian stores approved responses in a structure you define. You set expiration dates, track where each entry is used, assign review jobs, and control who can see and edit what. Version control keeps a history of past wording. What it does not do is keep that content current on its own: there is no live sync from your source systems, so a person has to review and update entries on a schedule.


### **Reporting and dashboards**


Qvidian includes more than 70 ready-made reports, a drag-and-drop builder, and dashboards that track proposal outcomes and how content gets used. You can pull win rates and content metrics for leadership without building the reports yourself.


### **AI Assist**


AI Assist is the newest layer. It drafts responses from the approved library, rewrites them for tone and length, applies your terminology, and reads an incoming RFP to help with a go or no-go decision.


### **Collaboration and approvals**


You assign questions to named people, route approvals through set stages, and track status across the team, so a large bid with many contributors stays coordinated in one place.


### **Microsoft Office and integrations**


Qvidian connects to Salesforce and Microsoft Teams, and offers Word, Excel, and PowerPoint add-ins. The Word add-in lets your team draft in Word and have responses populate in the document’s formatting.


### **Permissions and audit trails**


Role-based permissions and audit logs control who can access what and record every change, which security and compliance teams need for sign-off. Exact certifications vary by contract, so confirm them with Upland during evaluation.

## **Qvidian ratings, pros, and cons**


Qvidian has a long review history:[4.3/5 on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/upland-qvidian/reviews) from 166 reviews, and[4.6/5 on Gartner Peer Insights](https://www.gartner.com/reviews/product/qvidian) from 8. The pros and cons below come from real review sentiment.


Pros Cons


Version control and a clear hierarchy, the feature reviewers name most; keeps a large library organized. The interface feels dated, and routine tasks take more clicks than they should.


Built-in reporting is broad, with 70-plus prebuilt reports and dashboards. Loading new content is slow, and the library often opens in a second window.


The Word, Excel, and PowerPoint add-ins drop responses into your house format. Search misses the right phrase, and the filters are weak.


You assign tasks to the right person and track review and sign-off in one place. The platform can run slow, and some reviewers hit features that broke after an update.


Customer success gets steady praise for being knowledgeable and quick to help. AI Assist is early, and reviewers want it stronger and better tied to the library.


AI Assist adds generative drafting, tone edits, and RFP analysis. Pricing is premium and quote-only, with nothing lighter for a small team.


**Fact to know**
In a[Gartner survey](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2021-11-02-gartner-survey-finds-60-percent-of-employees-experience-frustration-with-new-software) , 60% of workers said software had frustrated them in the past two years, and many then used it less. For a tool reviewers call dated, that is the real risk: when people use it less, you lose the value you paid for.


## **Qvidian user reviews: what customers say on G2**


G2 reviewers like Qvidian’s library, version control, and support, and criticize its dated interface and search. Here are four reviews in their own words.


[Sean N. (3.5/5)](https://www.g2.com/products/upland-qvidian/reviews/upland-qvidian-review-12235075) likes "the library in Upland Qvidian where I can store answers and they are easily accessible," but finds " **user-friendliness lacking, especially in terms of providing directions for first-time users.** "


[Piers E., a Principal Bid Manager (4.5/5](https://www.g2.com/products/upland-qvidian/reviews/upland-qvidian-review-12222538) ), values being able to "assign tasks directly to stakeholders across the bid team," but says he " **would like to see more AI capabilities in Upland Qvidian** ."


[Noreen M.](https://www.g2.com/products/upland-qvidian/reviews/upland-qvidian-review-12816131) , a Contract Technical Editor at a mid-market company (4.0/5), rates the "version control and hierarchy, which is quite valuable for me," and wishes " **the search functionality could be improved, particularly around the filters.** "


[Sono N.](https://www.g2.com/products/upland-qvidian/reviews/upland-qvidian-review-12512588) , a Proposal Systems Administrator at a mid-market company (5.0/5), credits a support team "always available to assist and answer questions as well as being very knowledgeable," and notes that **some areas, such as Upland Analytics, feel "more complex and not as necessary" for her team today** .

## **Qvidian pricing at a glance**


Qvidian keeps pricing off its site. Expect a per-named-user license on an annual or multi-year contract, plus a one-time implementation fee to migrate content and set up the library. Two things drive the number: how many seats you license, and the implementation that lands in year one. Check out detailed[Qvidian pricing](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/qvidian-pricing) guide.


## **Who Qvidian is right for, and who should switch**


It comes down to one question: does the library and reporting outweigh the daily friction for your team? Use the two lists to place yourself.


**Qvidian still fits if you:**


- Run a large, established proposal team with a deep library and someone who owns it
- Rely on strict version control, permissions, and detailed reporting to answer to the business
- Work mostly in Microsoft Word and want responses to land in your house format
- Have the budget and time for a paid, multi-week implementation


**Look at alternatives if you:**


- Want first drafts you can trust, grounded in approved content with gaps flagged, not AI you check line by line
- Want your content kept current automatically, not through manual uploads and scheduled cleanup
- Need the team productive in days, not weeks of training on a heavy interface
- Would rather pay by usage than a seat count that climbs with headcount.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is Qvidian used for?


Teams use it to manage and respond to RFPs, DDQs, security questionnaires, RFIs, and SOWs from a content library, with review and approval handled in one place and often driven from Microsoft Word.


### Who owns Qvidian?


Upland Software acquired Qvidian in 2017 for about $50 million. Upland sells it today as Upland Qvidian, inside its wider portfolio.


### Can you try Qvidian before buying?


Not on your own. Qvidian has no self-serve trial, so evaluation means a guided demo and a sales conversation before you see it working on your content.


### How long does a Qvidian rollout take?


Plan for weeks, not days. Migrating content, configuring the library, and wiring up integrations is a paid implementation, so budget ramp-up time and a content owner alongside the license.


### Is Qvidian still being updated?


Yes. Upland still develops it, most visibly with Qvidian AI Assist for generative drafting, RFP analysis, and tone and length editing on top of the library.


### What should I compare Qvidian against?


Start with Inventive AI, Responsive, Loopio, and AutogenAI, set out in the table above, and pick by what you need most: AI-native drafting, an enterprise module set, or a managed library with a lighter lift.
